detailed_rationale:
Sterlite Technologies (STL) makes optical fibre, cable and connectivity products for telecom and, increasingly, AI data-centre infrastructure. The quant inputs (ROE -0.1%, PE ~475x, value score 13.7/100, 3y revenue CAGR -11.8%) describe a company still digging out of the 2022-24 telecom-capex winter and a stretched balance sheet - but this is now materially stale relative to what has actually happened. FY26 (year to March 2026) already showed the turnaround taking hold: revenue grew 39% YoY to Rs 4,745cr, PAT turned positive at Rs 56cr, net debt fell from Rs 1,350cr to Rs 1,128cr (net debt/equity improved to 0.50, net debt/EBITDA to 1.3x), and the open order book rose 67% YoY to Rs 7,309cr on ~110% growth in order intake. That alone would argue for cautious optimism. What has happened since is a step-change: Q1 FY27 (quarter to June 2026, reported 24-Jul-2026) delivered revenue of Rs 1,910cr (+87% YoY), EBITDA of Rs 397cr at a 20.2% margin (already at management's FY27 target, +720bps YoY), and net profit of Rs 197cr versus just Rs 10cr a year earlier. The open order book has since jumped again to Rs 18,618cr, anchored by a landmark ~US$1.11bn (~Rs 9,271cr) multi-year award to supply optical connectivity products for next-generation AI data centres (FY27-FY29), and the company used a Rs 1,500cr QIP to become net debt-free.

Taken together, this is not the same company the trailing quant ratios describe. The quant PE of ~475x is built on the thin/near-breakeven FY26 earnings base (Rs 56cr); rolling forward the four most recent quarters (FY26 full year less Q1 FY26, plus Q1 FY27) implies trailing PAT closer to ~Rs 240-250cr, which brings the effective trailing multiple down to roughly 100-110x on the same market cap - still not cheap, but a different order of magnitude, and one that is falling further each quarter if the AI-data-centre order book converts to revenue as guided. The QIP that funded the debt-free balance sheet did dilute existing shareholders, which tempers - but does not erase - the per-share improvement. Structurally, STL now sits at the intersection of two demand drivers: continuing telecom fibre capex and a genuinely new, large, high-visibility AI data-centre connectivity order book, which is a qualitatively different (and larger) addressable market than STL had access to a year ago.
recommendation_rationale: The quant Sell is anchored on trailing ratios (near-zero ROE, ~475x PE, negative 3y revenue CAGR) that reflect the company's 2022-24 trough and its still-thin FY26 earnings base - but the most recent actuals (Q1 FY27: revenue +87% YoY, EBITDA margin already at the 20% FY27 target, PAT of Rs 197cr vs Rs 10cr, net-debt-free balance sheet, and an order book that has roughly doubled again on the back of a $1.11bn AI-data-centre award) show a company that has already moved past the point those trailing numbers describe. This is a case where using the better live figures (per the desk's stale-data convention) materially changes the picture: the effective trailing PE is closer to ~100-110x than 475x, margins are already at target, and leverage is gone. That is still not a cheap stock, and execution/customer-concentration risk on the large single AI-datacentre award is real, so this is not a Buy-grade re-rating call - but the balance of evidence no longer supports a flat Sell. Rescuing to Hold.
summary: Sterlite Technologies has moved from a leveraged, loss-making turnaround story to a net-debt-free company hitting its margin targets early, backed by a rapidly growing order book that now includes a large, multi-year AI-data-centre supply contract. The scorecard's trailing valuation ratios look extreme because they are based on last year's thin earnings base; on the latest quarter's run-rate the picture is far more reasonable, though still not inexpensive and dependent on continued execution. We move this to Hold rather than Sell.
positive_para: The turnaround is now backed by hard numbers, not just narrative: Q1 FY27 revenue nearly doubled YoY, EBITDA margin hit the 20% FY27 target a year early, PAT swung to Rs 197cr, and the balance sheet went from net-debt to net-cash via a Rs 1,500cr QIP. The order book has roughly doubled in a single quarter to Rs 18,618cr, anchored by a ~$1.11bn multi-year AI-data-centre connectivity award - a genuinely new, large demand pool layered on top of STL's traditional telecom-fibre business, not merely a recovery to old levels.
negative_para: Even after the re-rating in the earnings base, the stock is not cheap on a normalised basis, and the growth is now concentrated in a smaller number of very large orders - the AI-data-centre award in particular carries customer-concentration and execution risk over its FY27-FY29 delivery window. The QIP that fixed the balance sheet also diluted existing shareholders, and the trailing 3-year revenue CAGR is still negative, a reminder of how far the business fell before this recovery began. Any slippage in data-centre capex spending or in converting the order book to billed revenue would remove much of the case for the recent re-rating.
reverse_dcf_judgment: On the stale trailing base (~Rs 56cr FY26 PAT) the ~475x quant PE looks impossible to justify. Rolling forward to the most recent four quarters (~Rs 240-250cr trailing PAT) puts the effective multiple closer to ~100-110x, which still requires several years of continued high growth (order book conversion, AI-data-centre ramp, margin holding near 20%) to justify on a reverse-DCF basis - plausible given the quantified Rs 18,618cr order book, but not a bargain. Judgment: fair-to-rich on the updated earnings base, down from clearly rich on the stale base; the QIP dilution and single-award concentration are the main risks to monitor.
